subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` now, and should existing no-override subagent/cron sessions continue including hook-loaded allowlist files?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but choosing the config surface and whether to break current hook-extra behavior affects session context and upgrade compatibility beyond what automation should decide.

options.title: Preserve legacy defaults, accept opt-in tiers
options.body: Keep current no-override hook-extra behavior unchanged, apply root-only filtering only for explicit `minimal` and `standard` tiers, then document and test the upgrade contract.

options.title: Accept root-only no-override filtering
options.body: Merge the root-only legacy change intentionally, but require maintainer-approved release notes, docs, and migration guidance because existing hook-extra setups can lose context.

options.title: Pause the config surface
options.body: Defer this PR behind a broader bootstrap/context-selection design that covers tiering, session filtering, lightweight mode, and hook extras together.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy defaults, accept opt-in tiers
recommendation.body: Keep current no-override hook-extra behavior unchanged, apply root-only filtering only for explicit `minimal` and `standard` tiers, then document and test the upgrade contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history on subagent bootstrap limiting and bootstrap resolver ownership.
